thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 Alert — Dedicated pool 'marigold-prod' reporting GPU capacity exhaustion for tenant MarigoldCorp. Current metrics: GPU util 98%, queue length 230, 503 spikes. Alert rule: dedicated.pool.gpu_exhaustion. Incident id: INC-20260315-01.

emma_oncall: Oncall here, picking this up. Paging SRE and infra. @kiran @infra-jen can you join?

kiran: Joining. Any customer-facing reports?

customer-success-aly: Customer opened a support ticket (78921) — they see intermittent 503s and very slow responses. They've escalated to account team. Said it started ~10m ago.

infra-jen: Looking at autoscaler events — pool marigold-prod was pinned (min==max) at 16 GPUs. No autoscale triggered. Why was it pinned? Pulling pool config now.

eng-runtime-mike: Also seeing a sudden jump in KV cache misses for the tenant and long-running embedding batches from a job ID 0x4fef. Could be a runaway batch job saturating GPU memory.

ops-robert: If there's a runaway tenant job we can throttle or suspend their low-priority batch queue. Do we have per-tenant job kill/limit controls available in this pool?

infra-jen: We do, but throttling requires coordination — we can limit concurrency for tenant via quota knobs. However, that won't free already allocated kernels. Immediate option: temporary burst capacity (manual) or move routing to quantized variants.

emma_oncall: Can we get an estimate on burst availability and approval path? Need to weigh SLA impact vs costs.

infra-jen: MarigoldCorp has burst allowance up to +8 GPUs but policy requires manual approval from product or ops lead for >+4. Current available credits: 6.

product-lina: Given customer is enterprise and this is user-facing SLA violation, I approve up to +4 GPUs for up to 3h. Approve now so infra can action.

kiran: I second. Approving manual burst +4g for 3h. infra-jen please proceed and document reason.

infra-jen: Running scaling command now:

```
# redwoodctl (internal)
redwoodctl pools update marigold-prod --scale +4 --duration 3h --reason "P1 MarigoldCorp burst approval"
# returned: operation pool-ff12ab scaling -> in_progress
```

incident-bot: Scaling operation pool-ff12ab initiated (+4 GPUs). Provisioning estimate ~3m.

ops-robert: While GPUs provision, I'm going to apply an emergency routing policy to prefer the lower-memory quantized model variant to reduce per-request memory pressure. This should reduce kernel footprints.

eng-runtime-mike: Agreed. I'll flip routing for Marigold to m-marigold-quant and lower concurrency cap. Command:

```
redwoodctl routing set marigold-prod --policy prefer-variant:m-marigold-quant --concurrency 120
```

infra-jen: Scale event completed. Pool capacity now 20 GPUs (was 16). New nodes registered: gpu-node-44..47.

kiran: Monitoring metrics: queue length dropping from 230 -> 60 over last 5m, 95th latency improving from 2.4s -> 0.9s, 503 rate down to baseline.

customer-success-aly: Propagated update to customer: "We activated temporary burst capacity and routing changes to restore service. Engineers are monitoring; we'll follow up in 1h with a technical summary." Customer responded: thanks and asked about next steps to prevent recurrence.

emma_oncall: Good. Decision: keep burst for now but plan to ramp down after traffic stabilizes. We need an action item: investigate why autoscaler was pinned and why tenant started heavy batch without quota checks. Assign to eng-runtime-mike.

product-lina: Also need a billing note for the burst charge and an operational note for account team. I'll take billing comms.

eng-runtime-mike: Created follow-up ticket PROD-8345: "MarigoldCorp dedicated pool exhaustion — autoscale pinned, batch job throttle gaps, routing fallback improvements". Assigned to eng-runtime team.

ops-robert: I put a temporary quota on tenant's batch scheduler to limit concurrent embedding jobs to 6. Command executed: `schedulerctl tenant marigold --max-batch 6`

infra-jen: Noted pool config change: removed min==max pin for marigold-prod; set min 12 max 24 with autoscale policy driven by 95th latency and queue length. Committed in infra repo: `infra/pools/marigold-prod.yaml`

kiran: Monitoring for 20m window. If metrics remain stable and queue < 50 for 10m, we'll plan scale-down of the burst capacity and mark incident mitigated.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation checkpoint at +12m: queue 38, GPU util 72%, 503 rate baseline.

emma_oncall: Approve scale-down in 2h unless regression. Keep customer updated. Final actions:
- eng-runtime-mike: postmortem draft and autoscale improvements (PROD-8345)
- infra-jen: add automated guard for pinned pools to alert earlier
- product-lina & customer-success-aly: customer comms and billing note

product-lina: I'll prepare customer-facing post-incident summary and include recommended config changes to prevent future pinning.

customer-success-aly: Customer confirmed errors subsided and is satisfied with the update. Will request follow-up call to review.

kiran: After 2h check: stable. Initiating scale-down now:

```
redwoodctl pools update marigold-prod --scale -4 --reason "End of emergency burst - stable"
```

infra-jen: Scale-down completed. Pool back to 16 GPUs. All routing policies reverted to default except concurrency cap still at 120 for 30m.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident INC-20260315-01 marked resolved at 4265018567. Postmortem ticket PROD-8345 created.

emma_oncall: Great work team. We'll circle back for RCA and close with the customer after postmortem. Closing thread. :thumbsup:
